name: Kumal
confidence_why: The only statement on Kumal stress is a single garbled line in Poudel's 2008 Nepali-language MA thesis on Tanahun Kumal, which puts stress on the first word of the sentence and on the "first word" of the word (presumably its first syllable), and none of the five other works consulted (Gautam 2000; Gautam, Parajuli & Yadava 2011; Rai, Rai & Thokar 2013; Kumal 2018; Kumal 2019) says anything about stress, so the record stays undetermined and word-initial stress is no more than a guess.

new_statements.translation: 13. In the Kumal language, when a sentence is pronounced, stress (aghat) generally has to be placed on the pronunciation of the first word of the sentence. That stress appears on the first 'word' [sic; evidently meant: first syllable/letter] of the word.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: opened (99 pp, PDF metadata Author 'Rukmani Poudel') and the saved page scan printed p. ३२ = p. 32). Item १३ of the numbered list reads exactly as quoted: 'कुमाल भाषामा वाक्यको उच्चारण गर्दा प्रायः वाक्यको पहिलो शब्दको उच्चारणमा आघात दिनुपर्दछ । त्यो आघात शब्दको पहिलो शब्दमा देखिन्छ ।' The Preeti->Unicode text (. line 883-884) carries the same sentence (only converter artefacts, ो rendered as ा+े). The list is headed '२.७.६. कुमाल भाषाका विशेषता' (. line 839, printed p. 31) and runs items 1-17; item 13 is the only prosodic remark (item 16 is about strong nasalization, 17 about sound-change processes). No phonology chapter elsewhere; a full-text search for stress/accent आघात/बला…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Impressionistic: prominence falls at the beginning: the first word of an utterance carries the stress, and within the word the stress sits on its initial syllable (if the evident slip 'first word of the word' is read as 'first syllable of the word').
new_statements.domain_note: Framed at sentence level (utterance-initial word), then located word-initially; a one-line remark in a list of 17 'features' in a Nepali-literature-department MA thesis, no phonological analysis, no examples. Variety: Kumal of Gandyaulitar/Dhorphirdi, Tanahun district. The feature list appears modelled on Sharma Paudyal 2043 VS (Palpa/Nawalparasi Kumal), which was not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Poudel 2008 describes the Kumal spoken in Gandyaulitar and Dhorphirdi, Tanahun district (Gandaki); Glottolog kumh1238 has no dialect nodes. The Jazyki mira sketch (silent on stress) draws on Arghakhanchi and Nawalparasi Kumal (Parajuli 2000, Gautam 2000); Sharma 1986 covers Palpa/Nawalparasi. All are the same language, Kumal = Kumhali [kra].

sources.note: Sec. 2.7.6 'features of Kumal', item 13, p. 32: when a sentence is pronounced, stress (aghat) is generally placed on the first word of the sentence, and that stress appears on the first [syllable; text literally says 'first word'] of the word. sources.note: Nothing on tone or stress is visible. The Academia.edu abstract (English, seen via the search index) says only that the paper 'outlines the sketch grammar of Kumal, a minor Indo Aryan language spoken in the Terai and inner terai regions of Nepal'; a Nepali-medium ruprekha normally opens with a varna/dhvani (sound-system) section, so a phoneme inventory is likely and a suprasegmental remark (aghat/balaghat 'stress', sur/tan 'tone') is possible but unconfirmed. No tone is expected for this Indo-Aryan language; at most a stress note like Poudel 2008's.
